auth.named: A credential already on this computer
auth.document: A key file I will paste (Google service account)
auth.chain: However this computer already signs in

intro1: The clouds a data flow can read. Set an account up here once, and any flow can point it at that cloud's files or its log events.
intro2: This page holds the credential and nothing else: which service a flow uses, and which bucket or log group, are chosen while you build it, from the lists the account can see. Requests go to your cloud from this computer, and a key you paste is kept in this computer's keychain rather than in the file beside it.
name: Name
foundFrom: Found on this computer, from {source}. Nothing is copied: picking one stores its NAME, and the credential is read when a flow runs, so it stays where you manage it and keeps working when you rotate it.
found: Found on this computer. Nothing is copied: picking one stores its NAME, and the credential is read when a flow runs, so it stays where you manage it and keeps working when you rotate it.
nothingFoundFrom: Nothing found on this computer from {source}. Type a name if you have one, or paste a key instead.
nothingFound: Nothing found on this computer. Type a name if you have one, or paste a key instead.
storedNotShown: The stored key is not shown, here or anywhere: nothing in the app can read it back out.
storedPaste: Stored. Paste again to replace it.
pasteWholeFile: Paste the whole file. It goes straight to this computer's keychain, is never written beside the account, and nothing in the app can read it back out.
chainNote: Uses whatever this computer already has: environment variables, a signed-in session, or the role a machine is running as. Nothing is stored by the app.
regionStorage: A starting point, not a constraint: listing your buckets does not depend on it, each one carries its own region, and a log group asks for one on the flow.
regionOther: A starting point, not a constraint: a flow chooses the region it reads.
endpointHelp: The address of your storage: Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Ceph, or anything else that speaks the S3 API.
addressByPathHelp: What most self-hosted storage needs. Without it the name goes in the host name, and a server that does not do that fails as a name-not-found, which reads as a broken network.
